stem: A 58-year-old woman with cirrhosis develops yellowing of her skin and eyes. In the healthy liver, bilirubin is processed by hepatocytes and excreted into which of the following structures?

options.label: A
options.misconception: The blood-supply channel is being cast as the excretion route.
options.explanation: Sinusoids deliver blood to the hepatocytes and contain phagocytic Kupffer cells; excretion of bilirubin runs in the opposite direction, into the bile canaliculi.

options.label: B
options.misconception: The inflow vessel is being cast as the excretion route.
options.explanation: The portal vein brings nutrient-rich blood to the liver; bilirubin leaves the hepatocyte through the biliary tree, not back into the venous inflow.

options.label: C
options.misconception: The exchange space is being cast as the excretion route.
options.explanation: The spaces of Disse lie between sinusoid lining and hepatocytes and mediate exchange with blood; bile, carrying bilirubin, drains into canaliculi on the opposite pole of the cell.

options.label: D
options.misconception: The blood outflow is being cast as the bile outflow.
options.explanation: Central veins collect processed blood from the sinusoids; bilirubin destined for elimination travels with bile through the canaliculi to the gut.

options.label: E
options.misconception: None; hepatocytes excrete bilirubin into the bile canaliculi.
options.explanation: Hepatocytes process nutrients, toxins, and waste materials carried by the blood, and materials such as bilirubin are processed and excreted into the bile canaliculi.

context: Learning objective: hepatocyte polarity. Blood flows through sinusoids (with phagocytic Kupffer cells) past hepatocytes to central veins; hepatocytes process nutrients, toxins, and waste, excreting bilirubin into bile canaliculi that feed the biliary tree. Failed excretion produces jaundice.
imageCaption: Bilirubin: spleen Hb breakdown -> unconjugated (albumin) -> hepatic conjugation -> bile -> gut bacteria -> urobilinogen/stercobilin; some urobilinogen -> urine.
